notes.wakayima: Apwoyo, the hare: the same word as thank you.
notes.fisi: Ongwen, the hyena; also a common name.

guidebook.intro: Folktales: **Apwoyo** the hare (the same word as “thank you”), and the Ganda legend of Kintu and Nnambi, told in Acholi.

tips.title: Ododo man pwonyowa ngo?
body: Every tale ends with its lesson: **Ododo man pwonyowa ngo?** (what does this story teach us?) **Pwonyowa ni ryeko loyo teko** (it teaches us that wisdom beats strength).

tips.title: Apwoyo and Ongwen
body: In Acholi tales **Apwoyo** the hare is small and clever, and **Ongwen** the hyena big and greedy. Apwoyo always wins by a **bwola** (trick).

culture.title: Why the hare is called thanks
body: Acholi children laugh that **apwoyo** means both hare and thank you. Ask an elder for the tale of how the hare tricked the other animals; every family tells it a little differently.
